task:
COLONY PLANNER S3a.1: ADD ASTEROID BELTS TO THE PLAN BODIES RESPONSE AND RECORD THE OWNER'S BELT RULE. BACKEND + DOCS ONLY. DO NOT TOUCH THE GENERATED CLIENTS (Claude regenerates them afterwards).

Owner rule (2026-10-31): colony sites are built in an asteroid BELT itself (if the system has one), never in its individual belt clusters. Belt clusters are bodies in V3 canonical data (`body_type` belt cluster); belts are rows of `{schema}.rings` with `kind = 'BELT'` attached to a parent body (`body_pk`). Today `GET /api/v1/plan/systems/{system_id}/bodies` (listV3PlanBodies, apps/api/src/routers/plan.py) returns the clusters but not the belts, so the planner has nothing to build on.

1. apps/api/src/routers/plan.py
   - Add model `PlanSystemBeltV1(PlanModel)`: `belt_id: str` (the ring_pk as a decimal string), `name: str` (rings.name, e.g. "<system> A Belt"), `parent_body_id: str` (rings.body_pk as a decimal string), `ring_type: str | None` (v3_vocab.ring_type.display_name via rings.ring_type_id; null stays null), `reserve: str | None` (the reserve vocabulary display_name via rings.reserve_type_id — find the vocabulary table name in apps/importer/src/v3_spansh/adapter.py VOCABULARY and sql/v3; null stays null), `mass_mt: float | None`, `inner_radius_km: float | None`, `outer_radius_km: float | None`.
   - Add `belts: list[PlanSystemBeltV1]` to `PlanBodiesV1` (after `bodies`), ordered by ring_pk.
   - Fetch them with ONE more parameterised query on the same resolved schema, wrapped in `_bounded`, filtered `system_id64 = $1 AND kind = 'BELT'`, LEFT JOINing the two vocab tables. Keep reading only canonical relations plus v3_vocab/v3_meta (no v3_derived, v3_app, v3_spatial), keep the existing three queries and every existing field unchanged, and keep `has_rings` meaning RING rows only.
   - An unknown system still returns 200 with empty `bodies` and empty `belts`.
2. tests/test_plan_bodies_postgres.py — extend the existing PostgreSQL 18 test (same fixture loader): for a fixture system that has BELT rows (find one in tests/fixtures/ratings_v4_sources via the loader; if none has a belt, insert one belt row inside the test the same transaction-safe way the existing test handles a BELT-only body, or the way other canonical tests mutate fixtures), assert `belts` equals what a direct query of `{schema}.rings` (kind BELT) + vocab gives, in ring_pk order, with null vocab ids staying null; assert RING rows never appear in `belts`; assert an unknown system gives `belts == []`. Keep every existing assertion.
3. tests/test_plan_router.py — the static no-v3_derived/v3_app/v3_spatial SQL check still passes; add an assertion that the OpenAPI schema for PlanBodiesV1 contains `belts`.
4. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md — in section 2 point 1 and section 5.3, add in plain words: sites go on bodies or on an asteroid belt (if the system has one); individual belt clusters cannot be built on, so the planner shows them only as information under their belt; a belt's slots start unknown and are entered by the commander. Add one line to section 10 (owner answers) dated 2026-10-31 recording the rule.

VALIDATION: ruff (both commands as before), `python -m compileall -q apps`, `python -m pytest -q tests/test_plan_router.py tests/test_cpe_boundary.py`, `python -m pytest -q tests/test_plan_bodies_postgres.py -rs` (collects and skips cleanly without RATINGS_V4_VALIDATION_DATABASE_URL; Claude runs it against PostgreSQL 18 afterwards), then the backend unit suite exactly as CI runs it, reporting counts. SUMMARY: changed files, the new SQL, which fixture system has a belt (or how the test creates one).
